raw.assessment: The incumbent coordinates named groups, room reservations and staffed key collection while supporting telephone and in-person access. Repeating 90-minute bookings plausibly support predictability, but that benefit was not measured. Eleven groups obtained weekly bookings; administration exceeded two hours in two observed weeks, and three access conflicts occurred. The limiting observation is that 68% aggregate reservation coverage does not establish usable spare capacity: six declined requests targeted Tuesday or Thursday evenings, acceptable alternatives were unrecorded, and only one room has a piano. Missing needs and equipment data prevent assessing the 90% target or attributing unmet demand to scheduling alone.

openings.claim: Would assigning existing capacity against complete acceptable windows and equipment requirements meet demand, or do compatible requests exceed capacity?
openings.delta: Distinguishes recoverable allocation mismatch from scarcity at specific times and in the piano room; aggregate vacancy and lateness cannot distinguish these explanations.
openings.prediction: An allocation mismatch would permit a feasible reassignment that meets at least 90% of stated needs and every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement; a compatible-capacity bottleneck would leave identifiable overlapping demands unsatisfied even after reassignment.
openings.probe: Use each contact's short conversation to record weekly needs, acceptable windows, minimum useful duration and necessary equipment. Attempt a paper allocation within the existing rooms and hours, preserving the dated performances and weekly entitlement. Count only usable building rehearsal time; undocumented outside rehearsals do not establish success. Include conversation and scheduling time in administration totals.
assumptions: Contacts can state their groups' needs accurately.
Feasibility on paper requires later confirmation through attendance and access records.

openings.claim: A single authoritative reservation ledger with explicit read-back of each booking or change may reduce conflicting room expectations.
openings.delta: Addresses the observed calendar disagreement while testing whether the other double-arrival conflicts also originate in recording or confirmation failures.
openings.prediction: If inconsistent reservation state drives conflicts, double expectations should decline after ledger reconciliation and confirmation; conflicts despite matching confirmed entries would implicate other causes.
openings.probe: Keep telephone and desk changes available. Record each accepted change once in the authoritative paper ledger, read back room, date and time, and mark the online copy's update time. Over eight weeks record conflicts, whether confirmations agreed, and total administration minutes; judge against fewer than two conflicts and the two-hour weekly average.
assumptions: Staff can consult the authoritative ledger when issuing keys.
Confirmation and copying can fit the administration budget; this remains to be measured.
This change retains existing equipment, fees, opening hours, performances and weekly access entitlements.

raw.assessment: The observations support investigating allocation and change coordination, but do not establish that sufficient compatible capacity exists. Aggregate vacancy cannot demonstrate satisfaction of equipment-specific or evening demand. Both proposed interaction benefits are hypotheses.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross elicited acceptable windows, equipment and required rehearsal duration with protected 60-minute cores plus requested extensions at the request-to-room allocation interface. Flexibility information could make shorter cores useful without converting longer rehearsal needs into apparent successes.
openings.delta: Recording preferences alone leaves inherited 90-minute boundaries; shortening bookings alone may expose time nobody can use. Joint allocation could pack compatible requests into gaps and reserve piano capacity for verified needs.
openings.prediction: Against both single-mechanism schedules, the combined schedule meets more complete stated needs within acceptable windows, while retaining every requested weekly minimum and both performances.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or in-person conversations to collect actual needs. On the same eight-week demand, compare inherited allocation, preference-aware 90-minute allocation, flexible-duration allocation retaining inherited starts, and the combination. Count fully met needs, guaranteed minima, equipment mismatches and preparation minutes; reject schedules violating constraints.
assumptions: Some groups can use different starts or durations; this is unmeasured.
Jointly feasible minimum slots exist within the two rooms and staffed hours.
A 60-minute guarantee is not automatically a fully met rehearsal need.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross a queue of preauthorized acceptable replacement slots with one authoritative desk ledger at the change-commit interface. A released slot can trigger one confirmed reassignment before synchronized calendar copies are issued.
openings.delta: A queue alone can propagate stale availability; a ledger alone does not identify who can use a release. Their interaction could convert changes into usable rehearsals with fewer repeated negotiations and conflicting expectations.
openings.prediction: The combination produces more accepted reassignments than the ledger alone and fewer conflicting confirmations than the queue alone, without increasing administrative minutes per change.
openings.probe: Replay documented changes with contacts' stated permissions under queue-only, ledger-only and combined rules; measure accepted placements, conflicting confirmations and handling time. Confirm real changes by phone or in person. Never release a weekly minimum without a confirmed replacement; lock performances and existing opening hours.
assumptions: Contacts can preauthorize alternatives without repeated negotiation.
The desk can maintain the authoritative ledger and refresh copies within the two-hour weekly administration ceiling.

openings.claim: Test allocation mismatch versus compatible-capacity scarcity, including whether elicited flexibility combined with protected 60-minute cores and requested extensions improves packing.
openings.discriminator: Aggregate vacancy proves neither feasibility nor usable capacity; preference information and shorter durations may help only jointly.
openings.fit: Z1 preserves constraints; A1 remains uncertain pending feasible minima and useful durations.
openings.probe: By phone/desk collect needs, windows, equipment and useful durations. Compare inherited, preference-aware 90-minute, flexible-duration inherited-start, and combined schedules for eight weeks. Measure fully met needs, minima, equipment mismatches and preparation time; identify overlapping unmet demand.
openings.uncertainty: Contacts' accuracy, duration/start flexibility and feasible weekly minima are unverified; paper feasibility needs attendance/access confirmation. A minimum slot or undocumented outside rehearsal is not proof of met need.

openings.claim: Test authoritative-ledger read-back against conflicting expectations, then its interaction with preauthorized replacement queues for usable released slots.
openings.discriminator: Ledger consistency addresses stale state; queues identify eligible replacements. Matching confirmations despite conflicts imply other causes.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints; retain phone/desk changes, lock performances/hours, and replace any released weekly minimum before release.
openings.probe: Replay documented changes under queue-only, ledger-only and combined rules; measure placements, conflicting confirmations and handling time. Record accepted changes once, read back room/date/time, timestamp refreshed copies and confirm replacements. Track eight-week conflicts and total administration.
openings.uncertainty: Preauthorization, desk/key access to the ledger and affordable copy/confirmation work remain unverified.

post_distill.decision: Probe both hypotheses; reject constraint violations. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, equipment, no new fees and performances. Success requires at least 90% usable needs met, every requested weekly minimum, fewer than two conflicts and average administration at most two hours/week, including elicitation.
